mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following comparisons of scientists correctly matches their contribution to the historical development of cell theory?

options.A: Robert Hooke – discovered cells in cork and coined the term “cell”; Matthias Schleiden – proposed that all plants are composed of cells.
options.B: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek – formulated the three tenets of cell theory; Theodor Schwann – discovered microorganisms in water.
options.C: Rudolf Virchow – stated that all cells arise from pre‑existing cells; Robert Hooke – observed cell division in animal embryos.
options.D: Matthias Schleiden – discovered the nucleus; Antonie van Leeuwenhoek – proved that cells can arise spontaneously.

mcqs.answer: Robert Hooke – discovered cells in cork and coined the term “cell”; Matthias Schleiden – proposed that all plants are composed of cells.
mcqs.explanation: Hooke first observed cell-like structures in cork and introduced the term “cell”. Schleiden later proposed that all plant tissues are made up of cells, a key step toward the cell theory. The other options mix up contributions or attribute incorrect discoveries.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly states the cell theory as accepted today?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: Cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter; all cells have a nucleus; plants are not composed of cells.
options.C: Only multicellular organisms consist of cells; animal cells can divide without DNA replication; viruses are cells.
options.D: The cell is the smallest unit of life but not the functional unit; cells can be created de novo under laboratory conditions.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: The modern cell theory has three core statements: (1) all living things are made of cells, (2) the cell is the fundamental unit of structure and function, and (3) cells arise only from pre‑existing cells. Options B, C, and D contain false statements that contradict the accepted theory.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best describes the difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms?

options.A: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all life functions, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells that perform specific functions.
options.B: Unicellular organisms have cell walls, while multicellular organisms never have cell walls.
options.C: Multicellular organisms can only be plants, whereas unicellular organisms can be only bacteria.
options.D: Unicellular organisms reproduce only by binary fission, while multicellular organisms reproduce only by seeds.

mcqs.answer: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all life functions, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells that perform specific functions.
mcqs.explanation: In unicellular life a single cell carries out all metabolic activities, whereas multicellular life shows division of labor among different cell types. Options B, C, and D are inaccurate generalisations.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an accepted exception to the original cell theory?

options.A: Viruses are considered cells because they contain DNA.
options.B: Mature red blood cells in humans lack a nucleus.
options.C: Plant cells can divide without a cell wall.

mcqs.answer: Mature red blood cells in humans lack a nucleus.
mcqs.explanation: The original cell theory stated that all cells have a nucleus, but mature mammalian erythrocytes lose their nucleus to maximise space for hemoglobin. Viruses are not cells, plant cells always retain a wall during division, and bacteria are unicellular.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Define the cell theory and distinguish it from the earlier concept of spontaneous generation.

options.A: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and all cells arise from pre‑existing cells; it rejects spontaneous generation which claimed life could arise from non‑living matter.
options.B: Cell theory claims that cells can appear spontaneously in broth; spontaneous generation states that cells are the smallest unit of life.
options.C: Cell theory says only plants are made of cells; spontaneous generation says only animals are made of cells.
options.D: Cell theory denies that cells have nuclei; spontaneous generation asserts that nuclei are formed spontaneously.

mcqs.answer: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and all cells arise from pre‑existing cells; it rejects spontaneous generation which claimed life could arise from non‑living matter.
mcqs.explanation: The cell theory’s three tenets directly contradict the older idea of spontaneous generation, which held that life could emerge from non‑living material. Options B‑D misrepresent both concepts.

mcqs.question: A researcher observes that a newly formed cell always appears adjacent to an existing cell during tissue growth. Which principle of cell theory does this observation illustrate?

options.A: All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.C: Cells are the smallest unit of life but not functional.
options.D: Cells can be created without division.

mcqs.answer: All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: The observation that new cells develop only next to existing ones exemplifies the principle that cells originate only from other cells. Options B, C, and D describe ideas that are not part of the cell theory.

mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is an example of a multicellular organism?
mcqs.explanation: Humans are composed of many specialized cells forming tissues and organs, fitting the definition of multicellular. Amoeba, Paramecium, and yeast are unicellular.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: A student notes that mature mammalian red blood cells lack a nucleus and mitochondria, yet they function in oxygen transport. Which refinement of the cell theory does this observation support?

options.B: Some specialized cells may lose organelles to perform specific functions.
options.D: Only plant cells have cell walls.

mcqs.answer: Some specialized cells may lose organelles to perform specific functions.
mcqs.explanation: The loss of nucleus and mitochondria in erythrocytes is a recognized refinement: certain cells discard organelles to optimise their role. Options A, C, and D are incorrect statements about cell theory.
